title: 📈 Monday data: More AI, more justice?
text: 📈 Monday data: More AI, more justice? Exponential View Subscribe Sign in 📈 Monday data: More AI, more justice? Everyone’s got a lawyer now Azeem Azhar and Nathan Warren Oct 05, 2026 ∙ Paid 41 1 3 Share Latest in our AI Investment Brief: An update on AI revenues + what’s happening with AI spending. In England and Wales, 60% of defendants in defended county court claims this year did not have a lawyer . In the US, more than nine in ten consumers sued for debt face the case without one . AI may give some of them a new way to argue their case. In Australia, Greg Baker, a computing academic, used AI to challenge his employer’s refusal to make his casual job permanent, and the Fair Work Commission ruled in his favor – an early example of a self-represented litigant winning with help from AI agents. Around 0.6% of all Claude use in May was for lawyers’ tasks , ranking 38th of 718 occupations, ahead of accountants but well behind programmers and writers. Four-fifths of these queries were people asking about their rights or what the law means. Continue reading this post for free, courtesy of Azeem Azhar.
